llm.summary: This skill is an offline health log manager, but it is advertised as a BMI calculator and stores sensitive health-adjacent notes persistently without strong privacy controls.

dimensions.detail: Using a local data directory is proportionate for an offline tracker, but the stored content can include sensitive health or goal information.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains a markdown skill file and one local bash script; no remote payload retrieval, dependency installation, tool replacement, or privileged install behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime commands are broader and less structured than the stated BMI purpose, and the documentation includes generated-looking command/output rows that do not clearly explain the actual behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The script creates persistent plaintext logs under ~/.local/share/bmi and records activity history, but it does not set restrictive permissions or provide retention, deletion, or privacy controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md description promises BMI calculation and body-composition charting, but the inspected script only stores and displays free-form text entries across categories such as log, track, goal, weekly, milestone, and trend.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if you expect real BMI calculations or charts, because it mainly saves free-form notes. Avoid entering sensitive health details unless you are comfortable with plaintext files being kept under ~/.local/share/bmi, and consider hardening or deleting those files manually if used on a shared system.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the artifact claims BMI calculation and charting, while the script implements generic local text logging and retrieval.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the script header and help text present a BMI health toolkit, but no BMI-specific computation or chart generation is implemented.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: the command set is mostly category-based note logging rather than structured BMI, weight, or body-composition processing.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: local persistence is disclosed and expected for offline tracking, but sensitive plaintext health-adjacent records are retained without clear privacy, permission, or deletion controls.
[T09] expected: Accepted as a medium local privacy issue: the script writes health-related logs without forcing owner-only directory and file permissions.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as low impact: search terms are quoted against shell execution, but grep option injection remains possible because the script does not use an end-of-options delimiter.
